title: Completeness as operadic localization
statement: Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The complete objects of $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ are exactly the objects local for the single map $s:E^1\to E^0$. The localization at the strongly saturated class generated by $s$ has as its inverted maps exactly the fully faithful and essentially surjective maps; its unit $A\to LA$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Here strongly saturated means closed under equivalences, two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and small colimits of arrows. If $\mathcal V$ is symmetric monoidal, its algebroid tensor $A\otimes B=\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product] carries a fully faithful essentially surjective map tensored with any identity to another such map. The map $A\otimes s$ is a local equivalence for every algebroid $A$. Thus completion is compatible with this tensor and the complete-object tensor is $L(A\otimes B)$.
